prerequisites: Ability to write medium-complexity programs using the C programming language

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the operating mechanisms of the Linux/Unix operating system.
Know and understand the methods for process management and inter-process communication in the Linux operating system.
Be able to program an application using correctly the basic tools provided by operating systems.
Be able to program complex applications, for example with modular or client-server architectures, exploiting Linux operating system's inter-process communication techniques.

Be able to independently understand technical documentation made available by operating system developer communities and major software companies, with particular reference to open source systems based on Linux.

syllabus_topics: Inter-process communication in Linux: unnamed pipes (6 hours)
Inter-process communication in Linux: named pipes (6 hours)
assessment_rules: Learning verification is carried out through practical tests distributed during the Operating Systems Laboratory. The practical tests will consist of three graded exercises performed during the laboratory, which will propose the use of UNIX/Linux system calls for process creation and communication in C language. After submitting the lab test, students must submit a new modified version that meets all the requirements declared in the test text within a time limit communicated during the test. Modified versions submitted after the deadline or that do not meet all requirements will be considered invalid and the student will not get the corresponding points. Each test will be evaluated with a maximum of 11 points, based on the number of requirements met by the version delivered at the end of the lab test, the correct use of UNIX/Linux system calls, and the extent of modifications between the version delivered at the end of the lab test and the modified one. The final grade is obtained as the sum of the scores obtained in each evaluated laboratory. In case of an insufficient final grade, students may take a practical test on all laboratory topics during the exam periods established by the academic regulations. The maximum score is 33. Those who obtain a total score of 32 or higher will receive a grade of 30 cum laude.
